In general, graph embedding methods that use multidimensional scaling (MDS) to handle millions of nodes avoid the O(n²) cost of full MDS on the all-pairs distance matrix. A common approach is landmark-based MDS: pick a small set of landmark nodes, compute distances only from those landmarks to all nodes, run exact MDS on the small landmark subproblem, and then place every remaining node by triangulation or distance-based projection against the landmark coordinates. Other variants use sparse or approximate distance matrices (for example, shortest-path distances within a neighbourhood) or Nyström-style low-rank approximations, so the cost scales roughly linearly in the number of nodes.
